samples: This program manages a small SQLite stock database with three reusable pieces: opening or creating the items table, adding a delivered amount to an existing product (failing if the product is unknown), and listing items at or below their reorder level, lowest stock first. Its entry point is a hardcoded demo rather than a general tool: it opens a fixed database file, records one fixed delivery of 500 units to a single product, and prints every item that still needs reordering (or a "nothing to reorder" message). It reads and writes local files, so it is worth using as a building block or example, but you would need to change the entry point to take your own file, product, and quantity.

This module manages a small SQLite stock inventory. It can open or create the database file and items table, add a delivered amount to an existing product (failing with an unknown-product error if it doesn't exist), and list products whose quantity is at or below their reorder level, lowest first. Its `main` is a fixed demo rather than a configurable tool: it always records one hardcoded delivery of 500 units of one product in a fixed database file, then prints the items still needing reorder or a "nothing to reorder" message. It is useful as a reusable set of inventory functions, but you would need to write your own entry point to use it for anything beyond that single delivery.

This module manages a small SQLite stock database. It can open or create the database file with its items table, add a delivered amount to an existing product's quantity (failing if the product code is unknown), and list products at or below their reorder level, lowest stock first. Its entry point is hard-coded: it opens one fixed database file, records a delivery of 500 units for one specific product, and prints the items still needing reorder (or a note that none do). It has no way to add products, so it only works on a database already seeded with that product, and you would need to write your own entry point for general use.

This program manages a small product inventory in a SQLite file: it creates the items table if needed, can add delivered stock to an item (failing if that product code doesn't exist), and can list items at or below their reorder level, lowest stock first. Its entry point is a fixed demo, not a general tool: it opens one hardcoded database file, records a delivery of 500 units for one hardcoded product, then prints the items still needing reorder, or a "nothing to reorder" message. It never adds new products, so it only works against a database already seeded with the right product, and on a fresh one the delivery step fails with an unknown-product error. The functions are reusable as a building block, but you would need to write your own entry point and way to load stock.

This program manages a small stock inventory in a SQLite file. It offers reusable functions to open or create the database, add a delivery to an existing product (failing with an unknown-product error if it isn't found), and list items at or below their reorder level, lowest quantity first. Its `main` is only a fixed demo, though: it always adds 500 units to one hardcoded product in a hardcoded database file and then prints the items still needing reorder (or a "nothing to reorder" message). So you would reuse the functions in your own program rather than run it as a general tool.
